Alice — appreciate the clear redlines and the focused asks. A few quick points from our side so we can align internal stakeholders before a sync: 

- Availability: 99.99% is aggressive for multi-region production traffic; our standard for hosted customers at the committed tier is 99.95% with a defined credit matrix. We can propose a regional split (99.99 for single-region Dedicated pools, 99.95 for cross-region fallback) or provide an availability SLA for API gateway while calling out best-effort for dependent third-party infra. I attached a proposed SLA amendment draft for your review.

- Service credits: we can work with a stepped credit schedule. Our standard cap historically is 50% for the billing month at the highest tier; we can discuss lowering to 30% with additional operational guarantees (e.g., response ladder, telemetry handoff).

- Response times: P1 acknowledgement in 15 minutes is feasible for our enterprise plan if we align on severity definitions. Remediation windows are harder to guarantee at 4 hours across all failure modes (especially hardware failures). We can commit to a response ladder (acknowledge/initial triage/patch) and offer a P1 mitigation SLA for infrastructure issues.

- Maintenance: 4 hours per region per month for planned maintenance is something we can explore for Dedicated customers; hosted multi-tenant will need a different carveout. We should capture planned vs emergency maintenance separately.

To expedite, can you confirm the following so we target the right artifact set for legal: 
1) Are you negotiating for hosted API or Dedicated capacity (or both)?
2) Will the order form include reserved capacity?

Per your compliance ask, attaching the SLA response matrix and pushing the audit pack. Internal owners @Marissa and @Kimberly — can you pull the SOC2 Type II, data retention policy, and KMS integration notes into the Drive folder linked below and confirm any exceptions?
